name: PRICEDISC
description: PRICEDISC returns the price per $100 face value of a security that is priced at a discount, such as a Treasury bill.
tldr: Calculates the price of a discounted security.

basicExample.description: Price of a discounted Treasury bill
basicExample.explanation: A T-bill with a 5% discount rate redeeming at $100 in one year is priced at $95.

advancedExamples.title: With actual/360 basis
advancedExamples.explanation: Basis 2 is common for money market instruments.

howItWorks: PRICEDISC calculates the price of a discount instrument using the formula redemption - (discount * redemption * days to maturity / days per year). It is used for zero-coupon and short-term instruments.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Discount rate is entered as a decimal.
Basis affects the day count and year length.

commonErrors.fix: Use DATE function or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: PRICEDISC works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between PRICEDISC and DISC?
faq.answer: PRICEDISC calculates price from a discount rate. DISC calculates the discount rate from a price.

faq.question: When is PRICEDISC used?
faq.answer: It is used for Treasury bills and commercial paper.
